caveats: Secondary expense reporting remains attributed and unadjudicated.

conclusions: The local-government connection is institutional:county legislative leadership, executive administration, economic development, budget oversight and workforce governance overlap with USC4AM governance or its operating host.
The centre has produced visible public outputs, but those outputs do not reconcile the state grant's drawdowns, county match, measurable outcomes or trip-level expenses.
The WXYZ findings warrant primary-record retrieval, not an inference of corruption or misuse.
counterarguments: Executive-committee service may be advisory and may not involve day-to-day spending decisions.
Missing conference documentation in a reimbursement packet does not prove the trip lacked a legitimate public purpose.
Aggregate investment and job outcomes may result from many activities and cannot be assigned to a particular trip without project-level evidence.
findings: David T. Woodward simultaneously chairs the Oakland County Board of Commissioners and serves as a public-sector member of USC4AM's executive committee.
USC4AM states that the executive committee sets strategic direction and guides key decisions.
David Coulter and Josh Hundt were named special advisers to the initial executive committee in 2022.
Dom Holmes now directs Oakland County Economic Development after more than five years at Automation Alley leading advanced-manufacturing investment initiatives.
Sean Carlson oversees Oakland County economic development, information technology, and management and budget, and is listed on the county workforce board.
USC4AM has documented completed outputs including a 2024 manufacturing report and a WEF/Purdue/Accenture innovation playbook.
WXYZ reported documentation gaps in county travel expense records, including a Milwaukee trip described as a USC4AM conference; the underlying records were not independently obtained.
data.framework: Separate formal authority, operational continuity, completed outputs, secondary allegations and unresolved primary records.
limitations: Underlying expense reports and receipts were not independently obtained.
USC4AM does not publish executive-committee minutes or a current decision log on the reviewed pages.
Public output pages do not identify which work was funded by the state grant or county match.
data.method: Compare current USC4AM governance and output pages with official Oakland County role records and a clearly attributed secondary investigation of public expense records.
data.question: Which current people connect USC4AM to Oakland County governance, and what documented actions or accountability gaps follow from those roles?
recommendations: Obtain the Milwaukee and Austin expense reports, receipts, travel approvals, conference agendas and attendee records.
Obtain the executed Michigan grant agreement, payment ledger, performance reports and Oakland County match documentation.
Retrieve USC4AM executive-committee appointment records, meeting minutes, conflict disclosures and decision logs.
Map current and former centre leadership transitions and compensation/funding sources.
Reconcile public outputs against the objectives in MSF Resolution 2022-080.
data.scope: USC4AM executive governance, Oakland County personnel overlap, current outputs and travel-expense documentation.
unresolved: Milwaukee conference name, agenda and attendees.
Austin conference name, agenda and attendees.
Woodward and Carlson travel approvals and reimbursement audit trail.
Executive-committee appointment dates, minutes and conflict disclosures.
Grant-funded versus independently funded USC4AM outputs.
Executed state and county agreements, payments and performance determinations.

summary: Current evidence places Oakland County officials inside the centre's strategy, operating and workforce interfaces while leaving transaction-level expense and grant-performance records unresolved.
title: USC4AM current local governance, outputs and accountability
